title: Adequate affinization of a product stack
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X$ be a finite-type algebraic stack over $k$, and let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space with $Y$ an affine $k$-scheme [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space, def-pc-scheme]. Finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $B=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X,\mathcal O)$, the ring of global sections of the structure sheaf on the stack product, and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The canonical morphism $\psi:\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X\to Z$, whose restriction to each smooth affine scheme chart is induced by pullback of global functions, is an adequate moduli space. Products are 2-fibre products of stacks; no quasi-finiteness or finiteness assumption is imposed on the diagonal.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, proof of (3) implies (1), printed pp.39--40, product adequately affine and its relative-Spec adequate moduli space; Proposition 4.2.1(1),(6), Lemma 4.2.3, Definition 5.1.1 and Remark 5.1.2 (the canonical relative-Spec morphism). Since Y times Y is affine, the displayed relative spectrum is Spec of global functions. Primary PDF read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Evaluating condition (2) of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] on the identity etale chart of $Y$ gives global power lifting on $\mathcal X$ for every surjection of quasi-coherent algebras. The same definition supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $\phi$. Hence [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion] makes $\phi$ adequately affine. The map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine (both schemes are affine). By the affine-example and composition clauses of [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-composition], $p:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is adequately affine.

Apply [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-affine-target-base-change] to $f=p$ and $h=p$ over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], $\mathcal W=\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack; the base-change lemma gives an adequately affine second projection $r_2:\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$. This is a base change along a stack morphism; the cited lemma explicitly allows it. No condition on $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(6), used in Theorem 8.3.2 product construction

proof.text: Compose $r_2$ with $p$. By [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-composition], $q=p\circ r_2:\mathcal W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is adequately affine. By [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism], $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion] over $k$: every section of every quotient quasi-coherent algebra on $\mathcal W$ has a positive power lifting globally.

Apply [lem-sfb-stack-affinization-qcqs] to $\mathcal W$ and its structural morphism $q$. Its canonical map $a_{\mathcal W}:\mathcal W\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(\mathcal W,\mathcal O)$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and induces the identity on global functions. Its scheme-chart characterization is exactly the stipulated $\psi:\mathcal W\to Z$, since $B=\Gamma(\mathcal W,\mathcal O)$. The global power lifting from step 3 and the identity $B\to\Gamma(\mathcal W,\mathcal O)$ satisfy all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-global-power-lifting-adequacy]. Thus $\psi$ is an adequate moduli space.

lean.statement: theorem adequate_product_affinization (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (hft : ∃ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U a ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom ∧ QuasiCompact U.hom) (Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsAffine Y.left] (φ : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj Y))) (hφ : IsAdequateModuliSpace F hF (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace Y) φ) : ∃ (hW : IsAlgebraicModuliStack (moduliSelfProduct F)) (B : CommRingCat.{u}) (e : B ≃+* moduliGlobalSectionsRing (moduliStructureSheaf (moduliSelfProduct F) hW.1.1)) (q : Spec B ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (ψ : BasedFunctor (moduliSelfProduct F) (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk q)))), (∀ (x : (moduliSelfProduct F).obj) (b : B), (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso B).inv ≫ Scheme.Γ.map (moduliRepresentableSchemeMap ψ x).op).hom b) = ((e b).1 (op x)).down) ∧ IsAdequateModuliSpace (moduliSelfProduct F) hW (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace (Over.mk q)) ψ
lean.note: The conclusion supplies a small ring presentation e : B ≃+* Γ(X×X,O), the canonical map to Spec B characterized on every total scheme object, and its adequacy. The small ring is existential output, never an added smallness assumption. The product is the recorded 2-fibre product of the recorded structural maps. No diagonal restriction.

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match: k field; finite type = exists smooth surjective scheme atlas with LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact (equivalent, no DM or smoothness added); Y affine k-scheme with the recorded IsAdequateModuliSpace hypothesis; product = recorded 2-fibre product of the structural maps over k. The global-function ring is presented by an output B : CommRingCat.{u} with a ring isomorphism e; smallness is true via restriction to the atlas, so no case is excluded. psi and q are pinned by the pullback characterization on every object (maps into Spec B are determined by their ring maps; e is injective), so this is the canonical affinization and not an arbitrary map; adequacy is stated for the same psi. Edge cases (empty stack, B = 0, any characteristic, non-DM stacks) are covered.
